title: Existence of an ordered centered toric tower lift
statement: Let $M$ be a fine torsion-free monoscheme with finite affine cover. Let $T$ be a finite normalized blowup tower of length $n$ with a specified $e_0:X_0\simeq\mathbf Q[M]$, whose coherent ordered centers have nowhere dense zero sets and are preserved by the lifted original component torus actions. Then there exists a centered toric tower lift of $(M,T,e_0)$ as defined in [def-trf-centered-toric-tower-lift-data]. This assertion supplies a lift with all ordered centers and equivariant monomial realization identifications; it makes no assertion of uniqueness or terminal smoothness.

source.place: Exposé VIII, 3.2.14--3.2.20, pp.105--106, with the saturated charts of 3.1.19--3.1.24, pp.101--102.

proof.text: Start with M at level zero, the inverse of the given base isomorphism, and its component torus action. These give the centered datum with no arrows or ideals. This works at length zero, and an empty base has no component conditions.

source.place: Exposé VIII, 3.2.14--3.2.20, pp.105--106, with the saturated charts of 3.1.19--3.1.24, pp.101--102.

proof.text: Assume stages through i have been lifted. Transport the given coherent center and original torus action across the current equivariant identification. The ideal comparison recovers the unique coherent monoid ideal realizing it. A component on which this ideal is empty would give a zero ring ideal, so its zero set would contain a nonempty clopen realization component, contradicting nowhere density. Coherence makes an empty stalk vanish on a neighborhood; comparison at the common generic point rules this out if any stalk in the component is nonempty. Thus the ideal is nonempty coherent everywhere.

source.place: Exposé VIII, 3.2.14--3.2.20, pp.105--106, with the saturated charts of 3.1.19--3.1.24, pp.101--102.

proof.text: Take the saturated blowup of that ideal. The blowup comparison supplies fine torsion-free finite-covered charts and the canonical identification with the normalized scheme blowup. Transport the latter along the current scheme isomorphism and identify it with the next level of T using T.blowup. The chart formulas identify the centers and the ordered arrows. Their original lattice coactions agree on localized overlaps and preserve the common dense torus, so they glue to the equivariant comparison required at the next level. Repeat n times; retain unit-center stages, including nontrivial saturations. No regularity or uniqueness conclusion is used.
